logline: A veteran engineer who has survived three decades at a Korean electronics conglomerate gets reassigned to HR - and learns that middle-age workplace survival requires an entirely different set of skills than the ones that kept him afloat.

bollymeter.basis: A mid-tier MBC workplace comedy anchored by Jung Jae-young and Moon So-ri - two respected character actors whose casting lent the show credibility above its modest premise. No formal critic aggregation available; editorial score reflects the strength of its leads and its unusually realistic portrayal of Korean corporate middle management.

seasons.review_body: On the Verge of Insanity occupies a specific and underserved niche in Korean television: the middle-aged workplace comedy that takes corporate politics seriously without turning them into melodrama. Jung Jae-young's Choi Ban-seok is a career engineer who has learned how to survive in product development over 30 years, then discovers HR operates by an entirely different social physics. Moon So-ri's Dang Ja-young runs HR with the kind of authority that comes from having already absorbed every backstab the organization can throw. The chemistry between them is the show's engine. The writing rarely wastes a scene on sentimentality, preferring dry observation. Without formal critical aggregation available, the show's reputation rests on its performances and its low-key precision - both of which reward patient viewers.

episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the central irony cleanly: Ban-seok is good at his job, and his competence is precisely what makes him a target. The show does not sentimentalize this.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Ban-seok's first day in the HR office, realizing that the rules governing his entire career do not apply here - played by Jung Jae-young with resigned bewilderment.
